papers.title: Joint analysis of the Macquart relation and the dispersion measure power spectrum: cross-covariance and redshift self-calibration
papers.abstract: The dispersion measures (DMs) of fast radio bursts (FRBs) trace ionised baryons along the line of sight, probing baryonic feedback. Two complementary observables can be constructed from an FRB catalogue: the DM-redshift (Macquart) relation of host-identified FRBs, and the angular power spectrum of the DM field of the full catalogue. Their joint analysis requires their cross-covariance. We derive it within the halo model and show it is a super-sample effect: only the monopole of an individual DM correlates with the angular power spectrum, yielding an exact, model-independent bound on the correlation coefficient. We validate the calculation against log-normal forward simulations of $10^4$ FRBs. For individual DMs, the correlation with the bandpowers is at the per cent level. Neglecting the cross-covariance changes the width of the $χ^2$ distribution by only 0.8 per cent, so the two observables can be treated as effectively independent for wide-area surveys. In a joint forecast with an LSST-like weak lensing survey, adding the Macquart relation tightens constraints on the physical baryon density by 32 per cent and on the mean host contribution by a factor of 4.1, while improving baryonification parameters by only about 5 per cent, indirectly through the host contribution. Finally, we show that the redshift distribution of FRBs without identified hosts, which enters every DM power spectrum, can be reconstructed by inverting their DMs with the jointly fitted mean relation without biasing the inferred parameters, whereas a 20 per cent error in the mean relation biases the DM power spectrum by up to 2$σ$ per band for $5\times 10^5$ FRBs.

papers.title: Analytic parametrisations of the scale dependence of proton parton distributions
papers.abstract: Parton distribution functions (PDFs) are non-perturbative inputs whose scale dependence is governed by the Dokshitzer-Gribov-Lipatov-Altarelli-Parisi (DGLAP) equations. Their numerical evaluation commonly relies on interpolation of tabulated grids. We discuss an analytic representation of collinear proton PDFs in $(x,Q^2)$, obtained by promoting the parameters of a standard $x$-space parametrisation to functions of the scale. The coefficients are reconstructed from the HERAPDF2.0 NLO set using machine-assisted fitting techniques, with sampling in $10^{-4}\le x\le 0.65$ and scales up to 1 TeV. The resulting ML-PDFs reproduce integrated distributions at the sub-percent level for most flavours, with deviations reaching about 1.5% for the strange quark at the highest scales. They satisfy valence and momentum sum rules at the percent level and reproduce representative $pp\toπ$ and $pp\toγπ$ cross sections within approximately 2% and 5%, respectively, in the kinematic regions studied. Compared with grid interpolation through LHAPDF, direct evaluation of the analytic expressions reduces the total Monte Carlo run time by about 11% and 30% in these two applications.

papers.title: Double Neutron Star Mergers and Fast Blue Optical Transients: A Circumbinary Disk Connection
papers.abstract: Post-common-envelope evolution (CEE) circumbinary disks (CBDs) form when part of the ejected envelope remains bound and circularizes around the stripped core and its companion. Leveraging results of scale-free hydrodynamical simulations, we develop a framework to model the effect of such disks on subsequent binary evolution, and implement it in the population synthesis code COMPAS. Applying our framework to double neutron star (DNS) merger progenitors, we find that CBDs generally induce substantial orbital shrinkage, changing the merging DNS population and lowering the overall merger rate. We explore an extensive grid of binary-evolution and disk models, and find that CBD interactions reduce the DNS merger rate by up to $28\%$, primarily through 'premature' mergers between the neutron star (NS) and the giant's core. These mergers may power luminous fast blue optical transients (LFBOTs), occurring at a fiducial rate of $\simeq11 \:\rm Gpc^{-3} \rm yr^{-1}$. Our results indicate that natal kicks contribute little to LFBOT offsets, and that they should be associated with young stellar populations, though not necessarily active star-forming regions. Since LFBOT progenitors would otherwise produce short-delay DNS mergers, CBDs further challenge DNS mergers as the source of early r-process enrichment. For surviving DNS mergers, accretion from the disk leads to higher chirp masses, potentially explaining the puzzling mass of GW190425. Our framework provides a general tool for studying CBD-binary interactions in post-CEE systems.

papers.abstract: Heavy-quark spin correlations in small-$x$ deep-inelastic scattering receive corrections beyond the back-to-back limit. We calculate the first nonvanishing correction at tree level for finite quark mass and finite $N_c$ in a homogeneous Gaussian target. The expansion through fourth order in the dipole sizes includes logarithms, contact terms and all interference contributions at that order. Comparison with the improved transverse-momentum-dependent approximation separates kinematic corrections from terms with additional insertions of the target current. Numerical integration of the unexpanded Gaussian kernel tests the approximation at 28 parameter points. Spin correlations differ between the two targets in all 12 kinematic comparisons; in one comparison both spin states remain separable. At fixed photon virtuality, the leading large-$P$ behavior of the fourth-order correction to the normalized transverse spin state is generically proportional to $m\ln P/P^3$. We also compare two fixed Gaussian targets using unpolarized momentum distributions and joint spin measurements. For a purely transverse photon, three narrow momentum bins and an ideal measurement of both spins along the common quark-momentum axis defined by the light-front boost, spin information adds 3.5-3.7 percent to the expected log likelihood ratio after the overall normalization is fitted. This increase depends on the spin analyzing power and bin selection. The calculation establishes a model-dependent effect, rather than an experimental sensitivity prediction.

papers.title: Reanalysis of GW170817 and GW190425 under the Goldilocks Prior
papers.abstract: Gravitational waves from binary neutron star mergers encode the properties of the densest matter in the universe, but recovering them accurately requires controlling biases introduced by the inference framework. The recently developed Goldilocks Prior incorporates correlations predicted by a large ensemble of candidate equations of state and broadens them according to the expected detector sensitivity. We apply this framework to GW170817 and GW190425 and find that the inferred component tidal deformabilities differ substantially from standard analyses. For GW170817, we infer both neutron stars to be more tidally deformable than previously reported, with the most probable value for the lighter star nearly doubling from $Λ_2\simeq215$ to $Λ_2\simeq443$ relative to the uniform-prior analysis. For GW190425, the Goldilocks Prior considerably reduces the range of allowed tidal deformabilities. We propagate the resulting event likelihoods to the dense matter equation of state using two complementary hierarchical methods, a strongly parametrized spectral representation and a broader semi-parametric Gaussian-process ensemble. For GW170817, both prior treatments yield consistent EoS constraints despite substantial differences in the inferred properties of the individual neutron stars. For GW190425, however, the EoS constraints differ beyond numerical scatter even after removing the source-level priors, showing that prior choice affects likelihood recovery for low-SNR events. papers.title: Stars Within Stars: The Interplay Between Main-Sequence Stars and Dark Matter
papers.abstract: Asymmetric dark matter may form self-gravitating macroscopic structures called dark stars if its microscopic properties give rise to sufficient effective pressure to counteract gravity. We study low-mass baryonic stars embedded within such dark stars, treating the baryonic and dark components as two gravitating fluids. The dark sector is assumed to be non-luminous and to interact with the baryonic star only through gravity, while the baryonic structure is computed using a realistic equation of state, opacity tables, and proton-proton-chain energy production. We find that the additional gravitational potential increases the luminosity at fixed baryonic mass, as the baryons must reach higher temperatures to maintain hydrostatic equilibrium. This lowers the minimum baryonic mass for hydrogen-burning configurations below the standard value of $\sim0.085M_\odot$. The resulting increase in luminosity can reduce the estimated main-sequence lifetime significantly, bringing low-mass configurations that would otherwise remain on the main sequence for hundreds of Gyr to cosmologically relevant timescales. We further show that photons escaping from the stellar surface undergo gravitational redshift determined by the global dark matter mass distribution. Consequently, extended dark star configurations can produce distinct observational signatures even when their outer regions have little effect on the intrinsic baryonic stellar structure, providing a potential probe of otherwise hidden dark structures.

papers.title: Confirming HSC strong lens candidates with DESI Spectroscopy. II. Analysis of 80 galaxy-scale systems with lens redshifts above 0.8
papers.abstract: The total mass distribution of galaxies provides a sensitive probe of the fundamental physical processes governing galaxy evolution, including gas inflow/star formation, AGN/SN feedback, galaxy merging, and the nature of dark matter. State-of-the-art cosmological simulations have therefore made extensive predictions for the evolution of the total-mass density slope. Interestingly, their predictions diverge significantly at high redshift, primarily due to differences in how these key physical mechanisms are implemented. However, measurements of the total-mass structure evolution have been largely confined to low and intermediate redshifts, leaving the regime where model predictions differ most significantly (z>0.8) largely unexplored. In the first paper of this series, we reported the discovery of 84 candidate strong-lens systems with lens redshifts above 0.8. In this work, we perform lens modeling of the 80 galaxy-scale systems to assess their lensing nature. Of these, 71 systems (approximately 90%) exhibit clear lensing features that are well reproduced by our lens models and are therefore classified as secure strong lenses. Another eight systems are classified as probable (5) or possible (3) strong lenses, based on the prominence of their lensing features and the quality of the lens modeling. One system lacking reliable lensing features in current imaging data is classified as a non-lens. Our analysis nearly triples the number of known galaxy-scale strong lenses at z_lens > 0.8, making statistical studies of the total mass structure of high-redshift galaxies possible for the first time. papers.title: Can absorption enhance differences between black-hole images?
papers.abstract: We investigate whether absorption can enhance morphological differences between images of different spacetimes, particularly when their critical impact parameters are similar. Near the first transition, the integrated difference between independently normalized images increases by $23.5$% on a common physical grid and by $46.6$% after rescaling by the respective critical impact parameters. Enhancement occurs across all three regular-black-hole families and over a broad range of the sampled flow parameters and viewing inclinations, although its magnitude and occurrence depend on the prescribed flow. Asynchronous brightness-peak transitions alone are insufficient to guarantee enhancement. These results suggest that the opacity dependence of image morphology may provide information complementary to the critical-curve scale, potentially helping distinguish spacetimes with similar characteristic shadow sizes. papers.title: The complex periodic variability of PKS 0301-243: hints of a supermassive black hole binary candidate
papers.abstract: In hierarchical galaxy formation, supermassive black hole binaries are a ubiquitous consequence of frequent galaxy mergers, yet subparsec binaries remain difficult to be confirmed. Such periodic signatures therefore motivate us to identify close binary candidates. Here, we report an optical periodicity of $269^{+13}_{-14}$ days in both Zwicky Transient Facility g and r bands of the blazar PKS 0301-243, with corrected global significances of $2.75σ$ and $2.18σ$, respectively. This signal persists over 7 cycles across a baseline of ~2000 days. We interpret this period as a possible modulation associated with the orbital motion of a supermassive black hole binary. A longer optical periodicity of $889^{+47}_{-46}$ days is identified in Katzman Automatic Imaging Telescope, with corrected global significance of $1.97σ$. The longer periodicity spans approximately 5 cycles over a baseline of ~4500 days, potentially associated with jet precession. Both periodicities are independently identified using multiple methods. A supermassive black hole binary incorporating a relativistic jet and a circumbinary disc could reproduce the observed light curve ensemble. papers.title: High precision timing of seven binary millisecond pulsars with the European Pulsar Timing Array
papers.abstract: Binary millisecond pulsars (MSPs) serve as exceptional astrophysical laboratories for a wide range of astrophysical studies, all of which rely on precise property measurements allowed by pulsar timing. In this paper, we present high-precision timing solutions for seven binary MSPs monitored by the European Pulsar Timing Array. By combining data collected from the five largest radio telescopes in Europe, as well as their coherently combined form, the Large European Array for Pulsars, we achieve phase-coherent timing solutions for all seven pulsars. We conduct a Bayesian timing and noise analysis on the combined data, yielding measurements of astrometric and orbital parameters with broadly improved precision, some reported for the first time. For PSRs J0125-2327, J1741+1351 and J2043+1711, we determine their distances and transverse velocities from astrometric measurements, and infer their masses via Shapiro delay measurements. Additionally, we examine the various contributions to the secular orbital-period variations for PSRs J0125-2327, J1125+7819 and J1741+1351, and estimate their kinematic distances. For PSRs J0125-2327 and J1741+1351, we detect the signature of annual-orbital parallax in the timing data. This allows us to derive a strongly favored, unique solution for the orbital ascending node and inclination angle for PSR J0125-2327, and a tightly constrained ascending node for PSR J1741+1351. Moreover, we use the orbital periods and their derivatives for several binary MSPs to place upper limits on gravitational-wave strain in both the sub-nanohertz and microhertz frequency regimes. Our results show that the orbits of binary MSPs could provide stringent constraints in microhertz range, thereby possibly complementing standard pulsar-timing-array analyses in the future.

papers.title: Survey of Surveys Data Release 3. Homogenised stellar parameters across nine spectroscopic surveys
papers.abstract: Large spectroscopic surveys have measured atmospheric parameters for millions of Milky Way stars, but differences in instruments, wavelength ranges, analysis methods, and assumptions introduce survey-dependent systematics that complicate their joint use. We aim to place effective temperature, surface gravity, and metallicity estimates from major spectroscopic surveys onto a common, externally validated scale, and to provide a homogenised catalogue for large-scale Galactic studies. We construct the calibration hierarchically. We first define an internal reference scale from the best-populated and best-overlapped surveys (APOGEE, GALAH, and LAMOST LRS), and model survey-to-reference corrections and their uncertainties with machine-learning regression. The scale is then extended to LAMOST MRS, Gaia RVS, RAVE, DESI, Gaia-ESO, and SEGUE, and anchored to high-quality measurements from the PASTEL database. The calibration reduces survey-to-survey offsets and improves consistency in independent overlap samples: independent calibration of GALAH and LAMOST LRS temperatures onto the APOGEE scale reduces their median offset from 44.5 K to 6.2 K. The final catalogue contains about 10.13 million stars, including 6.10 million in the recommended high-quality subset and 3.69 million in the metallicity-optimised subset. For the high-quality subset, Gaia benchmark stars give median residuals of 30 K in $T_{\rm eff}$, 0.03 dex in $\log g$, and $-0.02$ dex in [Fe/H]. The [Fe/H]-optimised subset gives median residuals of 0.003 dex against Gaia benchmark stars, 0.05 dex for globular clusters, and $-0.02$ dex for open clusters. As an example application, we confirm the presence of metal-poor stars on thin-disc-like orbits, including stars with [Fe/H] $< -2$, showing that the catalogue can be used to study rare Galactic populations on a consistent multi-survey scale.

papers.title: Systematic Study of Cosmic Rays in Star-Forming and Starburst Galaxies using Fermi-LAT and Multiwavelength Data
papers.abstract: The majority of $γ$ rays from star-forming galaxies (SFGs) and starburst galaxies (SBGs) are expected to originate from interactions between high-energy cosmic rays (CRs) and the interstellar medium, making $γ$-ray observations a powerful tool for probing CR populations and interstellar environments. Using 15 years of Fermi-LAT data, we conducted a systematic study of seven sources. The $γ$-ray spectra of the bright SBGs M82 and NGC~253 exhibit a decrease in energy flux below a few hundred MeV, suggesting a substantially smaller contribution from CR electrons than previously inferred. Detailed fits of the spectral energy distribution, which combine our GeV $γ$-ray measurements with reported radio and TeV $γ$-ray results, indicate that the electron-to-proton ratios in M82 and NGC~253 are comparable to that of the Milky Way. In contrast, energy densities of CRs in these two SBGs are 2.5--8 times lower than that of the magnetic field, unlike the Milky Way. For the nearby Local Group galaxy M31, we decomposed the $γ$-ray emission into two components, revealing a central source with a soft spectrum and a compact size of less than 0.33 degree, which indicates a considerable contribution from unresolved sources. Our new analysis also reduces the $γ$-ray fluxes of several SBGs, bringing all SBG sample members to levels comparable to or below the calorimetric limit, with calorimetric efficiencies ranging from 0.33 to 1.20. In contrast, all SFG sample members exhibit low efficiencies at the 10\% level. We developed a theoretical model of interstellar $γ$-ray emission that successfully reproduces the observed calorimetric efficiencies, providing a robust framework for interpreting and predicting $γ$-ray emission from SFGs and SBGs.

papers.title: Systematic Search for Cataclysmic Variables in Radio Surveys: First Radio Detection of IX Velorum
authors: David L. Kaplan Patrick A. Woudt
papers.abstract: We present a systematic search for radio emission from cataclysmic variables (CVs) across four wide-field radio surveys in the 0.7-4 GHz frequency range: VLASS; RACS; VAST; and EMU. We generated a reliable catalog of 2225 optically-identified CV candidates using a multi-stage cross-match, combined with systematic and manual verification; 1374 are matched to Gaia sources within the radio surveys' footprints. Among these, we detected six CVs in at least one epoch (at 1e16.5-1e17.5 erg/s/Hz, consistent with the typical population of radio-detected CVs); five had been detected in radio before. IX Vel, the closest nova-like CV, is detected in radio for the first time and shows quasi-persistent low-level emission across a 10 hr EMU (943.5 MHz) observation. Given most epochs detected no CV, we stacked images without radio detections to better constrain time-averaged brightnesses. We created co-added images and placed upper limits on low-level radio emission from each of the 423 individual CVs within the VAST footprint. To constrain the median brightness for the entire CV population, we combined all Gaia-matched CVs in each survey into single population-wide stacked images, detecting no statistically significant emission. Finally, we created population-wide image stacks of the CVs within 100 pc, using 14 epochs from 5 CVs in EMU to constrain their median persistent specific luminosity to <3e14 erg/s/Hz.

papers.title: Photometric eclipse-center variations over the long cycles of Magellanic double-periodic variables
papers.abstract: Double-periodic variables (DPVs) are interacting binaries with an orbital modulation and a longer cycle of uncertain origin. I searched for long-cycle-dependent eclipse-center variations in Magellanic DPVs and tested whether changing disk brightness can produce analogous shifts with fixed conjunctions. I analyzed Optical Gravitational Lensing Experiment (OGLE) photometry for 109 eclipsing-DPV candidates. In separate long-phase intervals, I measured centers of eclipses by profile fitting to local flux minima ($Q$) and by shifting a fixed eclipse template ($T$). A single synthetic semidetached DPV provided a separate numerical experiment. Of 49 curated systems with sufficient timing data, 27 show at least one $Q$ or $T$ modulation under the adopted procedure. Some selections depend on the fitting choice, but ten systems retain a selected $Q$ curve with all tested local functions and windows. Three have both estimators selected in both eclipses, without establishing whether conjunction times change. Using local color interpolation, 14 of 16 systems measured in both eclipses are redder at the deeper, phase-0 eclipse. In the artificial system, fixed conjunctions coexist with large photometric shifts and quadrature-brightness changes, although the large tilted-disk cases do not reproduce the selected observed crossing phases. Long-cycle-dependent photometric eclipse-center variations occur in a substantial fraction of the evaluable, curated sample, not necessarily of all DPVs. Circumstellar brightness changes can produce such shifts, but the single artificial system neither fits an observed DPV nor establishes disk tilt as the cause. Genuine conjunction-time changes remain possible in individual objects.

papers.title: The cold substellar frontier in JWST Extragalactic surveys: a robust parallax measurement yields the most distant known ultra-cold Y dwarf
papers.abstract: We present an analysis of JADES-GS-BD-5, an extremely cold Y dwarf identified in the JADES/GOODS-South field. Using multi-epoch JWST/NIRCam imaging spanning a $\simeq2$-yr baseline, we calibrate the JWST astrometry and obtain the first robust parallax measurement for a brown dwarf discovered in a JWST extragalactic deep field. We measure a proper motion of $μ_{\rm tot}=49.8^{+0.3}_{-0.3}$ mas yr$^{-1}$ and a parallax of $\varpi=15.7^{+1.4}_{-1.3}$ mas, corresponding to a geometric distance of $d=64^{+6}_{-5}$ pc, $\sim3\times$ further than that of the previously known most distant Y dwarfs with parallax-measured distances. We hence determine a tangential velocity of $v_{\rm tan}=15.0^{+1.4}_{-1.3}$ km s$^{-1}$, consistent with a Galactic thin-disk object. We find no evidence for binary acceleration, significant photometric variability, or a plausible host. The $J$-band spectral morphology of JADES-GS-BD-5 is consistent with existing Y-dwarf templates, while its extremely faint luminosity and overall near-infrared spectral profile confirm that it is one of the coldest dwarfs discovered to date. We therefore adopt a classification of $>$Y1, consistent with a NIRCam colour-based proxy of cY1.5. The robust parallax-determined distance allows us to determine its bolometric luminosity, $\log(L_{\rm bol}/L_{\odot})=-7.08^{+0.09}_{-0.09}$. Evolutionary modelling places JADES-GS-BD-5 in the planetary-mass regime and makes it a rare benchmark for the study of cold giant-planet atmospheres. Current atmospheric models fail to reproduce its SED in detail, pointing to the importance of disequilibrium chemistry and vertical mixing. Finally, we also report additional proper motion measurements for eight of the other nine known JADES Y-dwarf candidates, highlighting JWST extragalactic surveys as a powerful route to building a statistically useful, parallax-calibrated sample of Y dwarfs.
